nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules Block
nodes.rationale: Auto-generated and re-added by `next dev` via node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js. Warns that this Next.js version has breaking changes versus model training data, so the guides in node_modules/next/dist/docs/ must be read before writing code. Committing the block with the work keeps the tree clean because removing it only re-creates the uncommitted change.

nodes.label: Project Instructions Entry Point
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md contains only an @AGENTS.md include, so all project instruction content is single-sourced in AGENTS.md rather than duplicated.

nodes.label: Firebase Project Provisioning
nodes.rationale: Steps 1 to 5 must be done once before the app runs at all. Authentication is Email/Password with sign-up left closed, and the single operator account is added by hand under Authentication, Users.

nodes.label: Firestore eur3 Location Choice
nodes.rationale: Egypt to Europe is a much shorter trip than Egypt to any US region, and the location cannot be changed later without recreating the database.

nodes.label: Service Account Credentials
nodes.rationale: Three values from the downloaded service account JSON become FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID, FIREBASE_CLIENT_EMAIL and FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY. The private key keeps its quotes because its newlines travel through an environment variable as literal escape sequences and src/lib/db.ts converts them back. FIREBASE_WEB_API_KEY only checks the operator password at sign in and grants nothing on its own. The service account JSON bypasses Firestore security rules completely and is treated as the keys to the business.

nodes.label: Deny Everything Firestore Rules
nodes.rationale: firestore.rules denies everything because no browser ever talks to Firestore, only the server does through the Admin SDK, which bypasses rules anyway.

nodes.label: Composite Indexes And Rules Deploy
nodes.rationale: Firestore creates collections on first write so there are no tables or migrations, but the two composite indexes the admin lists sort by are declared in firestore.indexes.json and deployed together with the rules. An index created from a query error link must be copied back into the file so it is not lost at the next setup.

nodes.label: Local Firestore Emulator
nodes.rationale: Local development runs against the emulator so no service account key sits on a developer machine and nothing done locally can touch real customer data. With FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST set the Admin SDK talks to localhost and never authenticates; commenting the line out points at the real project.

nodes.label: InstaPay Recipient Variables
nodes.rationale: Customers copy NEXT_PUBLIC_INSTAPAY_ADDRESS and NEXT_PUBLIC_INSTAPAY_NAME straight into their banking app, so a typo is a misdirected transfer rather than a cosmetic bug and the values must be checked character by character.

nodes.label: Vercel Functions Pinned To fra1
nodes.rationale: vercel.json pins functions to fra1 to match the database location; serving from a US region makes every query cross the Atlantic twice. FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST must never be set in production because it would point the live site at a database that does not exist.

nodes.label: Backup Runbook
nodes.rationale: The free tier has no scheduled export and the documents hold wedding dates and customer phone numbers. npm run backup writes every invitation and review to backups/ with Timestamps rendered as ISO strings so the file can be restored without the Admin SDK. Scheduling must live somewhere the owner controls (Windows Task Scheduler, or a paid service), and the output must be copied off the machine that made it. A managed export to a Cloud Storage bucket needs billing enabled, which the free tier does not have.

nodes.label: ImageKit Free Plan Limits
nodes.rationale: Free plan gives 20 GB bandwidth per month and 3 GB storage; bandwidth resets monthly and storage does not. A bandwidth alert must be set well below the cap because on the free plan delivery stops rather than slows at the limit, which would take the photos off every live invitation in the middle of somebody's wedding.

nodes.label: Eight Music Files In public music
nodes.rationale: Eight tracks go in public/music and are not in the repo. npm run check:music reports what is present. Until the files exist invitations open silently and the mute toggle hides itself; nothing breaks.
nodes.norm_label: eight music files in public music

nodes.label: Reference What Runs Where
nodes.rationale: Database is Firestore in eur3 reached with the Admin SDK over HTTPS, credentials are a service account in three FIREBASE_ variables, local database is the emulator, indexes and rules deploy together, admin login is Firebase Auth with one account and a two week session cookie, and Vercel functions are pinned to fra1.

nodes.label: Invitation Theme Set v2
nodes.rationale: Produced by a 17-agent research workflow: market sweep, positioning brief, four independent concept panels, three judge lenses, canonical set. 55 concepts proposed, 12 selected, all palettes verified against WCAG AA. Nine are built and listed in src/themes/registry.ts; the legacy four remain renderable with listed false.

nodes.label: Coverage Not Score Selection Rule
nodes.rationale: Three judges produced overlapping but not identical top tens and the union was not taken. The chosen set is the smallest that puts one theme in every segment by occasion by ground cell the positioning brief names, gives each theme a structural device no other theme uses, and survives a mid-range Android. Several 8-scoring concepts were cut for redundancy and two 6-scoring concepts were kept because nothing else covers what they cover.

nodes.label: One Structural Axis Per Theme
nodes.source_location: Set rationale, the twelve structural axes
nodes.rationale: Each theme owns exactly one structural device and no other theme may borrow it: aperture, frame-as-measure, suspension and z-depth, continuous surface, field stack, horizon, dated leaves, ruled table, fold grid, off-centre column with a live ornament gutter, discrete objects, monolith. None duplicates classic's bordered panel, modern's centred column of hairlines, floral's rounded panel with corner sprigs, or midnight's invisible spine. Differentiation is satisfied by construction rather than by taste.

nodes.label: Light Ground Ladder And Two Dark Cap
nodes.rationale: Nine of twelve grounds are light because that is what this market buys and what the 300 EGP price anchors. The dark tier is deliberately capped at two objects rather than four, because a dark theme that reads as a recolour damages the two that do not. Khayamiya is the only fully saturated ground and maximalism is correct for a henna night and wrong everywhere else.
nodes.norm_label: light ground ladder and two dark cap

nodes.label: Contrast Token Contract
nodes.rationale: Every ink, muted and accent token in all twelve themes was computed against both its own bg and its own panel and all thirty-six pairs clear 4.5:1. Five judge-flagged tightnesses were fixed by changing the hex rather than by arguing. accentSoft is below 4.5:1 in every light theme by design and is declared ornament-only, per the house rule that a light-ground theme budgets a decorative accent and a separately darkened text accent.

nodes.label: Type Register Spread
nodes.rationale: Twelve distinct Arabic display faces and eleven distinct body faces, with Noto Naskh Arabic the only repeat. Amiri appears nowhere as a pairing face and Cairo appears nowhere. The register spread runs geometric Kufi, flat poster display, manuscript Naskh and contemporary display, so the set has four voices rather than one.

nodes.label: Amiri Quran As The Verse Face Only
nodes.source_location: Set rationale, type; per-theme font blocks
nodes.rationale: Amiri Quran appears in all twelve themes as the verse face for the Bismillah and Ar-Rum 21 only, declared as each theme's own verse token rather than inherited. This is stated as a correctness rule, not a style choice.
nodes.norm_label: amiri quran as the verse face only

nodes.label: Quranic Text Never Sits On A Pattern
nodes.rationale: Every theme suppresses its ground tile behind the Bismillah and verse block: the lattice goes to zero in mashrabiya, the ablaq tile in iwan, the pleat gradient in makhmal, the merlon border in khayamiya, and the verse sits on the palest band in ghouroub. Gold never touches the verse, because that is exactly where the hayba test fails.
nodes.norm_label: quranic text never sits on a pattern

nodes.label: Reduced Motion Rest State Contract
nodes.rationale: Every theme declares a prefers-reduced-motion rest state that is the finished state rather than a degraded one: the aperture already open, the arch legs fully drawn and the doors open, all parallax layers static with lamps solid, seams fully stitched from first paint. Nothing loops in any theme, and no scroll signature uses blur or filter.

nodes.label: Mid Range Android Performance Budget
nodes.rationale: Surviving a mid-range Android is a selection criterion, not a polish step. Consequences across themes: transform-only composited scroll signatures with no filters, hard element budgets enforced in the component rather than in a comment, pleat and lattice layers fixed at viewport height because a document-height gradient costs paint linear in page length, confetti counts reduced, and moire interference tested at high DPR before the pattern pitch is fixed.

nodes.label: Retire With listed false Rather Than Delete
nodes.rationale: Themes that have shipped are retired by setting listed false so existing invitations carrying that id still render. The legacy four remain renderable this way.
nodes.norm_label: retire with listed false rather than delete

nodes.label: Three Built Then Cut Themes
nodes.rationale: makhmal, sijill and lawh had their components, registry entries and eight orphaned typefaces deleted outright rather than retired to listed false. That is safe only because none of the three ever reached main, so no invitation in the database can carry one of those ids. Their specs are kept as a record.

nodes.label: Mashrabiya Theme
nodes.rationale: Owns the APERTURE axis: a full-bleed turned-wood lattice with content sitting in voids cut through it, never on a field. Consecutive voids alternate inline-start, centre, inline-end so there is no vertical axis at all. Ground lifted to a pale tone with a deep walnut lattice specifically to separate it from iwan's warm stone at picker thumbnail size. Usable measure inside a hexagonal void is 244px, not the 300px it looks. Spec only.

nodes.label: Iwan Theme
nodes.rationale: Owns FRAME-AS-MEASURE: the arch is the column, so no max-width token exists in the theme and the reading measure tapers from 342px to 286px over three haunch steps, capped at 28px total. Built and live. Cover opens as a two-leaf door on rotateY hinges. The no-photo state takes a muqarnas half-dome and is deliberately the better card, inverting the usual apology.

nodes.label: Qandeel Theme
nodes.rationale: Owns SUSPENSION AND Z-DEPTH, the only genuine third dimension in the set: everything hangs on plumb lines of an authored irregular length sequence across three depth planes differing in scale, opacity and colour temperature. Explicitly proposed as a replacement for midnight rather than an addition, because midnight's gold spine sits behind a centred column and cannot be seen. The no-photo substitution is invisible to the pixel. Spec only.

nodes.label: Makhmal Theme
nodes.rationale: Owns CONTINUOUS SURFACE: one uninterrupted pleated velvet field with seams instead of rules, and two seams that crop and displace content so the fabric is load-bearing on the layout. Its scroll signature is a one-pixel pitch difference between two gradient layers. Built and then cut, code deleted, because it never reached main.

nodes.label: Khayamiya Theme
nodes.rationale: Owns FIELD STACK: full-bleed saturated appliqué cloths with zero page margin, sewn seams, and no shared ground behind them. The only fully saturated ground in the set, targeting the repeat-purchase henna-night segment the product cannot currently sell to. Flat fill is a lint rule: one gradient converts it from sewn to printed and the theme dies. Spec only.

nodes.label: Ghouroub Theme
nodes.rationale: Owns HORIZON: six discrete fixed-height full-bleed bands, never one document-height gradient, with a moving line and content flipping above and below it. Targets the North Coast summer couple, the uncontested half of the calendar. Its accent was darkened to #93381f because four of the six band grounds are not tokens and a paragraph in a blend zone fails silently. Built and live.

nodes.label: Netiga Theme
nodes.rationale: Owns DATED LEAVES: a bound pad of labelled panel sheets on a board, each bound at the top by an accent header band, torn to the one day that matters. The most instantly recognised object in the set, aimed at the family-hosted traditional household. Spec only.

nodes.label: Sijill Theme
nodes.rationale: Owns RULED TABLE: unbroken full-width 1px rules at a strict 44px baseline pitch with label and value columns, the only genuinely tabular layout in the set. Positioned as the sober contract SKU for the observant household. Built and then cut, code deleted, because it never reached main.

nodes.label: Zarf Theme
nodes.rationale: Owns FOLD GRID, the only layout built on a fold rather than a flow: one sheet creased into three unequal panels whose creases are placed at content boundaries, so a long custom message cannot break the fold logic. Khatm was folded into it, and khatm's dotted-leader correspondence list belongs in its bottom flap. Spec only.

nodes.label: Hadiqa Theme
nodes.rationale: Owns OFF-CENTRE COLUMN WITH A LIVE ORNAMENT GUTTER: one hand-authored jasmine stem SVG split into eight sub-paths acts as an index of sections beside a permanently off-centre column. Proposed as floral done honestly, taking floral's slot rather than sitting beside a theme the brief has already retired, because painterly floral is out of reach and line work is the substitute. Built and live.

nodes.label: Rizma Theme
nodes.rationale: Owns DISCRETE OBJECTS: five overlapping ivory insert cards at five different measures on a warm grey table, and the only theme in the set where panel is lighter than bg. Delivers the paper-object idea with opaque cards and real contrast numbers, which is why it was kept over tayya's translucent vellum leaves. Built and live.

nodes.label: Lawh Theme
nodes.rationale: Owns MONOLITH: one continuous block on one fixed measure with no section breaks, dividers, panels or ornament between paragraphs. Its ground was warmed from limestone grey to ivory, raising ink from 10.21 to 12.81 on panel and answering the market judge's drab objection in the same move. Built and then cut, code deleted, because it never reached main.

nodes.label: Midnight Legacy Theme
nodes.rationale: One of the legacy four, still renderable with listed false. Its single structural idea, a gold spine, sits behind a fully centred column and is therefore invisible, which is the argument for qandeel replacing rather than joining it.

nodes.label: Floral Legacy Theme
nodes.rationale: One of the legacy four, still renderable with listed false. Its rounded panel with corner sprigs is the register hadiqa is meant to replace, since the brief has already retired painterly floral.

nodes.label: Classic Legacy Theme
nodes.rationale: One of the legacy four, still renderable with listed false. Its bordered panel is one of the four structural devices the new axes must not duplicate, and nothing in the new set replaces it.

nodes.label: Considered And Dropped Concepts
nodes.rationale: A record of what was cut and why, kept so salvageable components are not lost: shama as the third dark if the set ever grows, meeqat blocked on a running-order schema field that should ship first as a priced feature, hinna's trail cover gesture, khatm's dotted-leader list, tazkara's label-led details block, tiraz's Cormorant Unicase cross-script observation, and eighteen concepts rejected outright by at least two judges.

nodes.label: Meeqat Dropped Concept
nodes.rationale: An off-axis rail with content hanging from labelled timed nodes, extending into a running order. The only concept that answers what a guest actually asks. Cut because its scroll-drawn line at an inline offset is hadiqa's device and because the running-order content is not in the schema. The instruction is to ship the running-order field first as a real priced feature, then the theme.

nodes.label: Tayya Dropped Concept
nodes.rationale: Four overlapping translucent vellum leaves where the alpha-multiply overlap band is the divider. Cut on a defect of goods: at 0.82 alpha every one of its seven contrast tokens is notional, which breaks the colour contract rather than bending it. Revivable only if the composited leaf colour is computed once and entered into the token table as a real value.

nodes.label: Shama Dropped Concept
nodes.rationale: The highest-scoring cut concept, dropped purely on the rule that two excellent concepts in one segment in one register means one goes: it is a dark, gold, evening, one-lit-object card and qandeel already is that. Held as the third dark if the set ever grows.

nodes.label: qlty Brand Palette (Gold, Cream, Warm Grey, Dark Brown)
nodes.norm_label: qlty brand palette (gold, cream, warm grey, dark brown)

nodes.label: Traced-Vector Lockup (No Embedded Fonts or Rasters)
nodes.norm_label: traced-vector lockup (no embedded fonts or rasters)

nodes.label: qlty.events Brand Mark (app icon)
nodes.rationale: Vector app icon for the qlty.events invitation app. Source comment states it was 'traced from the brand artwork' rather than authored from scratch, so the geometry is a hand-traced reproduction of an existing logo rather than a parametric/regenerable shape. Composition: a rounded-square (squircle) badge containing a stylized calligraphic 'q'-like glyph with a swash tail, rendered as three stacked filled paths on a 136x137 viewBox.

nodes.label: Gold Badge Path (#b8924b)
nodes.rationale: Bottom layer: the rounded-square badge silhouette filled antique gold, with the glyph knocked out via fill-rule evenodd. Path coordinates run from -1.8 to 133.9 against a 0..136/137 viewBox, so the badge deliberately bleeds ~2px past the canvas edge to avoid a hairline gap when rasterized as a favicon.

nodes.label: Cream Glyph Path (#faf5ef)
nodes.rationale: Middle layer: the letterform itself, filled warm off-white/cream. Its outline is the same traced contour as the gold badge's knockout, re-emitted as a positive fill so the glyph reads as a solid cream shape rather than a transparent cutout.

nodes.label: Dark Brown Detail Path (#3b2a20)
nodes.rationale: Top layer: a very small dark-brown accent covering only the swash/crossbar junction region (x 85-97, y 48-55). It exists to restore contrast where the cream glyph and the gold badge outline overlap, and is invisible at favicon sizes.

nodes.label: Warm Gold-Cream-Espresso Brand Palette
nodes.rationale: Three hard-coded hex fills define the product's identity colors: antique gold #b8924b, warm cream #faf5ef, espresso brown #3b2a20. No CSS variables or currentColor are used, so the mark is theme-independent by design - it must render identically on light and dark browser chrome where a favicon has no theme context. This is the canonical source of the invitation app's warm/wedding-stationery color language.

nodes.label: Next.js app/icon.svg File Convention
nodes.rationale: The file's location and name (src/app/icon.svg) is not arbitrary: Next.js App Router treats a file named icon.* directly inside the app directory as the route-level favicon and auto-generates the <link rel="icon"> tag plus cache headers. Consequence: no explicit import or <head> markup references this file anywhere in the codebase, so static import-graph extraction will show it as an orphan even though it is a live build output.

nodes.label: Hand-Traced Vector Provenance
nodes.rationale: The leading HTML comment declares the artwork was traced from source brand artwork. Practical implication: the path data is one-decimal-place machine trace output with no named groups, ids, or semantic structure - it cannot be meaningfully hand-edited, recolored per-shape beyond the three fills, or animated. Any change to the mark requires re-tracing from the original artwork, not editing this file.

nodes.label: qlty.events Digital Invitations
nodes.rationale: Self serve mobile invitation builder for the Egyptian market: customer builds an invitation, previews it, pays 300 EGP over InstaPay, and gets a link to send guests on WhatsApp.

nodes.label: No Customer Accounts, Secret Token Access Only
nodes.rationale: No customer accounts exist anywhere in the codebase; access to an invitation is by secret token only. Keeps the product self serve with no signup friction and no customer credential surface.
nodes.norm_label: no customer accounts, secret token access only

nodes.label: Firestore as the Datastore
nodes.rationale: Deviation 1. The whole stack is Firebase: the Admin SDK against Firestore, with the same Firebase project also holding the operator login. The original spec had described a Postgres datastore accessed through an ORM with a pooled runtime URL and a direct migration URL; that plan was abandoned and no Postgres connection URL exists any more. Consequences: no schema and no migration step, a new field is simply absent from every previously written document rather than a column with a default, queries are weaker (in-memory filtering where SQL would have used ILIKE), and local development runs against the Firestore emulator.

nodes.label: Deny-All Firestore Rules
nodes.rationale: firestore.rules denies everything: no browser ever talks to Firestore directly, only the server does. Combined with the two composite indexes in firestore.indexes.json that the admin lists sort by.

nodes.label: Hand Written Data Model (src/lib/types.ts)
nodes.rationale: Written by hand because Firestore has no schema to generate from; it is the only description of document shape that exists.

nodes.label: In-Memory Admin Query Filtering
nodes.rationale: src/lib/admin-queries.ts filters in memory because Firestore cannot express the substring match a relational ILIKE would have answered directly; the comment in that file records what the workaround costs.

nodes.label: The One Page Flow
nodes.rationale: Replaced four routes (/build, /build/theme, /build/preview, /build/payment) with a single page at / that asks one question at a time. Every answered question collapses into a tappable row above the live one so everything the customer has told us stays on screen and any answer can be corrected in one tap without rewinding what follows.

nodes.label: Legacy /build Route Redirects
nodes.rationale: The four old paths redirect to / carrying their query string so /build?package=UNLIMITED still arrives with that tier selected. /build/status/<editToken> was deliberately not moved: it is where every paying customer lands and it is already inside messages that have been sent.

nodes.label: toPatch All-or-Nothing Rule
nodes.rationale: A patch is rejected whole by the server, so a half typed Google Maps link is left out of the patch rather than sent and refused. Every field that can be invalid is excluded in toPatch and nowhere else, keeping the exclusion logic in one place.

nodes.label: Date and Time Start Empty
nodes.rationale: The old form pre filled a date sixty days out, which is indistinguishable from a chosen date once stored. createDraft still writes that default, so the flow rather than the database is what prevents somebody paying for a day they never picked.

nodes.label: qlty_step Progress Cookie
nodes.rationale: Where a customer got to is a cookie, not a database column. clampFurthest refuses to trust the cookie past the first unanswered question, so a lost cookie costs a few taps but can never skip one.

nodes.label: Preview Dialog Mounted on the Unopened Cover
nodes.rationale: The preview is a full bleed dialog that mounts on the unopened cover and has to be tapped open, because audio.start() is only accepted by Safari while that tap is still on the stack.
nodes.norm_label: preview dialog mounted on the unopened cover

nodes.label: Audio Requires a Synchronous Tap
nodes.rationale: useInvitationAudio.start() must stay synchronous inside the open handler. Put an await before it and Safari stops treating it as user initiated, and the music silently never plays.

nodes.label: shadcn/ui Token Slots Pointed at Brand Values
nodes.rationale: Components are not themed at the call site; the shadcn token slots in globals.css are pointed at existing brand values so --primary is the gold the invitation uses as its accent and a plain Button comes out gold on cream.
nodes.norm_label: shadcn/ui token slots pointed at brand values

nodes.label: Theme Colours Must Use @theme inline
nodes.rationale: A plain @theme block resolves at build time, so --color-inv-bg: var(--inv-bg, #faf5ec) compiles to the literal fallback and every theme silently renders the classic palette. Went unnoticed while all themes were light and only became visible once a dark theme existed.

nodes.label: Classic Theme Composition
nodes.rationale: The two reference invitations flow as one column with the same flourish between every section; this card deliberately does not, so that it reads as its own thing.

nodes.label: Monogram Seal
nodes.rationale: Carries the couple's initials, leads the cover, and on the card sits between the two names where an ampersand would otherwise go.

nodes.label: Single Bordered Details Panel
nodes.rationale: Date, hour and venue are gathered into one bordered panel rather than three separately divided sections, because those are the details a guest reopens the card to check. Ornamental dividers are reserved for real changes of subject: three, not seven.

nodes.label: Formal Date Setting and formatEventDateParts
nodes.rationale: Weekday above, the day large between two rules, month and year below. formatEventDateParts exists to feed this layout.

nodes.label: Countdown as Four Rings
nodes.rationale: Rings rather than four filled tiles, so the countdown does not read as a row of interface buttons.

nodes.label: SupportButton WhatsApp Bubble
nodes.rationale: Floating bubble bottom right in WhatsApp green rather than the site's gold, because it has to read as WhatsApp at a glance. Pinned to the physical right, not the logical end, so it does not swap corners when the language changes. Carries the request id into the prefilled message on the waiting screen. Deliberately absent from the invitation and the preview: guests must never see it, and the preview is the customer looking at their own card exactly as a guest will.

nodes.label: InvitationView (no editToken, no id)
nodes.rationale: The public page carries no editToken and no id, neither in HTML nor in the props sent to the browser: the theme is handed an InvitationView built in src/lib/invitation-view.ts which has neither field.

nodes.label: Africa/Cairo Date and Time Resolution
nodes.rationale: Verified across Cairo daylight saving: August resolves to UTC+3 and December to UTC+2, so the countdown is right on both sides of the transition.

nodes.label: Arabic to Latin Slug Transliteration
nodes.rationale: Deviation 4, best effort. Arabic does not write short vowels, so src/lib/slug.ts works in three passes: Latin input passes through untouched, a dictionary of common Egyptian names covers most real traffic exactly, and anything else falls back to a character map that repairs an unpronounceable opening consonant cluster. It will still get some names wrong; the admin slug override at stage 14 is the backstop and until then a wrong slug is fixed in the database directly.

nodes.label: Arabic Diacritic Ranges Must Use \u Escapes
nodes.rationale: Combining marks are invisible in an editor, so a range that looks like it covers the tashkeel can quietly cover U+0621 to U+064A, which is every Arabic letter. That exact mistake was made in src/lib/initials.ts and silently returned an empty string for every Arabic name. Both mark regexes, in initials.ts and slug.ts, are now written as \u escapes.
nodes.norm_label: arabic diacritic ranges must use \u escapes

nodes.label: Never Force Direction on Text Containing Arabic
nodes.rationale: The numeric utility sets direction: ltr and belongs on bare digits only; applied to a mixed Arabic date string it reorders the date. Use bdi to isolate a Latin run without changing alignment.
nodes.norm_label: never force direction on text containing arabic

nodes.label: Bismillah Glyph Container Query Sizing
nodes.rationale: The glyph is about eleven times wider than its font size, so it is sized with a container query in the classic theme. Any new theme that renders it needs the same treatment or it runs off both edges of a phone.

nodes.label: No Double Hyphens in Customer Facing Text
nodes.rationale: Enforced in copy and comments; CSS custom properties are the exception because the language requires two hyphens.
nodes.norm_label: no double hyphens in customer facing text

nodes.label: satoriText Arabic Word Reversal
nodes.rationale: Satori reverses multi word Arabic and the direction property makes no difference, so satoriText in src/lib/og.tsx reverses the words on the way in to cancel it out. That only works for a line that is one phrase: a line mixing Arabic, a separator and digits has several bidi runs and comes out wrong however it is fed in, which is why the date, venue and occasion each get their own line.

nodes.label: Satori Arabic Font Compatibility
nodes.rationale: Satori rejects the contextual substitution lookups Amiri and Scheherazade New use for Naskh joining and cannot read variable fonts at all. Tajawal and Almarai were the only two of six candidates that worked; any font change must be rendered and looked at before being trusted.

nodes.label: ImageKit Photo Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Upload, HEIC handling, compression, EXIF stripping and the cropper. A synthetic photo has been through the whole pipeline: upload signature accepted, crop stored as coordinates, delivered at 49KB with no EXIF or GPS markers left in the bytes.

nodes.label: HEIC Decoding Unverified
nodes.rationale: HEIC has never been decoded. It is the iPhone default and the single most likely upload failure in this market, and it needs a real photo off a real camera roll, which cannot be done from a desktop.

nodes.label: Music Library Empty, Audio Unproven
nodes.rationale: No music file has ever played. The library is empty, so the fade in, the loop and the mute toggle are unproven. The mute toggle hides itself when a track file is missing rather than showing a control that does nothing.

nodes.label: Nothing Verified on a Physical Phone
nodes.rationale: Section 16 of the spec is not satisfied and only the owner can satisfy it. Three of the bugs found so far only appeared at human clicking speed.
nodes.norm_label: nothing verified on a physical phone

nodes.label: Backup Scheduling Not Automated
nodes.rationale: Deviation 2, the one open decision. npm run backup dumps every row to backups/, but the single daily Vercel Hobby cron is taken by the heartbeat and a Vercel function has nowhere durable to write, so the schedule has to live somewhere the owner controls. A choice must be made before taking real money because the Firestore free tier has no scheduled export at all.

nodes.label: Arabic Fonts Subset by Unicode Range
nodes.rationale: Deviation 3. Character level subsetting is unreachable because the largest text on the card is the couple's names, which are user input and unknown at build time. The Arabic and Latin unicode ranges are loaded instead of the whole face, and an Arabic card never fetches the Latin file.
nodes.norm_label: arabic fonts subset by unicode range

nodes.label: expiresAt Has No Policy Yet
nodes.rationale: Deviation 5. DEFAULT_EXPIRY_DAYS_AFTER_EVENT is defined as 30 days after the event in src/lib/constants.ts but nothing sets the field, because nothing activates an invitation until stage 7.

nodes.label: English Invitation Content Written Separately
nodes.rationale: Deviation 6. Arrived early because the theme is driven by direction and font variables rather than duplicated markup, so once the copy existed both languages rendered. It is written separately from the Arabic, not translated: the Arabic card carries the Bismillah, the verse from Ar-Rum and classical verse, while the English one uses 'Together with their families' and 'request the pleasure of your company'.

nodes.label: Hosting Families Line and Dress Code Removed
nodes.rationale: Deviation 0. Removed on request after the spec was written, and removed fully from the document type, validation schema, builder form, invitation and both dictionaries rather than hidden in the interface, so nothing carries a field that no longer means anything. Section 8.2 of the spec still lists both fields; the README is the newer instruction. Restoring either is a change to InvitationRecord plus a form field plus a section in each theme.
nodes.norm_label: hosting families line and dress code removed

nodes.label: Fourteen Stage Build Order
nodes.rationale: All fourteen stages are written and have run against a real Firebase project and a real ImageKit account; only HEIC decoding and audio playback remain unproven.

nodes.label: admin.qlty.events Subdomain Routing
nodes.rationale: The subdomain is handled in src/proxy.ts; locally the admin is just /admin.

nodes.label: Working On This Together (Contributor Guide)
nodes.rationale: Three people, one small codebase, one shared database.

nodes.label: .env Secrets Handling
nodes.rationale: The .env is not in the repository and never will be: it holds a live database password and the ImageKit private key. Values must come from the project owner through a password manager or encrypted message, not over WhatsApp or a chat window. Copy .env.example to .env; SETUP.md explains where every value comes from.

nodes.label: Firestore Emulator for Local Development
nodes.rationale: Local development runs against the Firestore emulator so nothing on a developer machine touches customer data. Commenting out FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST points at the live shared project where every write is immediately visible to everyone.

nodes.label: Firestore Has No Migrations
nodes.rationale: There is no schema to alter and no migration to run, so a shape change never fails loudly the way a missing column does. Adding a field to InvitationRecord leaves every already-written document without it, so new fields must be read back as optional and defaulted rather than assumed present.

nodes.label: src/lib/types.ts Is Hand Written
nodes.rationale: Nothing generates it because Firestore has nothing to generate from. It is the only description of document shape that exists, so it is accurate only for as long as contributors keep it accurate: update it in the same commit as the code that writes the new field.

nodes.label: Test Invitations Pile Up in the Admin List
nodes.rationale: Everything built shows in the admin's pending list alongside real customers, so test couples need obviously fake names to stop anyone activating one by accident.
nodes.norm_label: test invitations pile up in the admin list

nodes.label: Branch and Pull Request Workflow
nodes.rationale: Nobody commits to main directly once there is more than one contributor. On a team this size the review is less about catching mistakes than about two people knowing how each part works. Always run npm run typecheck and npm run build before pushing, because a failing build on main blocks everyone.

nodes.label: Phone Testing Against a Production Build
nodes.rationale: Over ninety five percent of traffic is phones, and the project has already produced five bugs invisible on a desktop and obvious on an iPhone within a minute, among them a cookie browsers silently discarded, autosave losing the last thing typed, and a timezone mismatch that stripped every button of its click handler for three hours each evening. Test with npm run build and npm start, then open the machine IP on port 3000 from the phone on the same wifi.
nodes.norm_label: phone testing against a production build

nodes.label: Dev Server Stale Chunk 404 on Phones
nodes.rationale: The dev server regenerates its JavaScript filenames on every file change. A phone has no hot reload connection, so it requests chunks that have already been replaced, gets a 404, and the page renders with every button dead. It looks like a catastrophic bug but is an artefact of the dev server.
nodes.norm_label: dev server stale chunk 404 on phones

nodes.label: Who Can Reach What
nodes.rationale: Code needs GitHub collaborator access; the database and admin need Firebase console access or the .env values; photo storage needs ImageKit dashboard access or the .env values; live deployment needs Vercel project access.

nodes.label: Single Operator Account, Public Signup Disabled
nodes.rationale: The admin has exactly one operator account and public signup is disabled. Additional admin logins are created by the owner from the Firebase console under Authentication, Users, Add user: the console can create accounts even with signup disabled, which is the point of disabling it.
nodes.norm_label: single operator account, public signup disabled
